rationale: The working tree is in exactly the state the skill's 'Aborting is a tool' section names: resolution went sideways, staged/unstaged hunks are interleaved, and it is no longer possible to distinguish deliberate rulings from accidental edits. An uncertain working tree is the thing you cannot afford to keep — pressing on would mean verifying and recording provenance against a tree whose contents I cannot vouch for, making every subsequent ruling unsanctioned drift. The traces are the work and they are already written down outside the tree, so they survive the abort at zero cost. Simulated plan: git merge --abort (restoring the pre-merge state and the return path), then restart the merge and re-apply each non-trivial hunk's resolution deliberately from the saved traces, staging each ruling as it is made, then run both origins' motivating checks and record per-hunk rulings in the merge commit message.

The skill's trace/provenance machinery (steps 2-5) is reserved for non-trivial hunks and does not engage here; per its own gate, trivial hunks are never traced, so no 'traced' field is claimed.
resolution: Take the formatter's side of the hunk (equivalently, resolve either side and re-run the auto-formatter), since both sides are token-identical and only the formatted layout differs; no intent exists to preserve or drop, so no per-hunk ruling or provenance record is required in the merge commit message.
